task: Recover the exact accepted playable project and make an immutable backup
why: Branch names and screenshots cannot identify the build the user actually approved.
complete_when: Record commit or full file-hash manifest, entry scene, engine version, save sample and matching capture; test restoration.

task: Map main, local, Drive and experimental branch ancestry
why: The Citadel, rig, art and dodge lines contain different features and assumptions.
complete_when: Publish a source-of-truth matrix with each branch head, dependency chain, approval status and integration destination.

task: Define the launch promise and first vertical slice
why: PoE-like combat is a design target, not an affordable commitment to PoE's whole content catalog.
complete_when: One-page scope names launch features, exclusions, player audience, session loop and G2 slice; expansion ideas remain separate.

task: Choose supported platforms, minimum hardware and input devices
why: Camera readability, renderer choice, texture budgets and UI depend on actual devices.
complete_when: Name CPU/GPU/RAM/storage/OS targets, minimum resolution, performance mode and mouse/keyboard/controller scope.

task: Choose offline versus online authority before architecture hardens
why: Multiplayer changes saves, combat authority, economy and operations, not just the connection menu.
complete_when: Decision record selects offline single-player or a separately budgeted network scope and defines future migration limits.

task: Establish a named decision log and source index
why: Contradictory hotkeys, camera estimates and duplicate latest documents cause rework.
complete_when: Every approved decision links its evidence and owner; estimates and draft art are labeled; repository and Doc versions agree.

task: Create a canon board from approved AOTL references
why: External ARPG references explain readability; they do not replace AOTL's identity.
complete_when: Board separates approved hero, city, UI and skill references from unapproved studies and records permitted variation.

task: Define shape, palette, material and lighting rules per region
why: A consistent world needs more than a single grading filter.
complete_when: Art bible specifies silhouette families, value hierarchy, surface wear, focal contrast and warm hub versus hostile-area treatment.

task: Build a matched-camera comparison scene
why: Close-up model renders can hide weak gameplay silhouettes and feet.
complete_when: Capture identical actors, arch, stairs and light in candidate pipelines at 1080p/1440p, with movement and combat footage.

task: Set a visual review rubric and rejection examples
why: Words such as polished or less AI are too vague for production acceptance.
complete_when: Review checks clear edges, coherent anatomy, clean surfaces, intentional detail, distinct skills and no generic haze/grain or distorted ornament.

task: Approve representative hero, enemy, prop and skill assets before batches
why: Repeating an unapproved style scales rework.
complete_when: Each category has an accepted engine capture, editable master, import preset and documented time-to-acceptance.

task: Separate technical, visual and integration approval
why: Import success cannot certify animation quality or a live scene.
complete_when: Asset registry records all three statuses independently; unapproved candidates cannot silently become default runtime art.

task: Calibrate projection from the supplied composition
why: Neither exact pitch nor focal length can be recovered uniquely from the image.
complete_when: Save a camera profile with measured actor screen height, pitch/yaw, projection, world scale and matched reference capture.

task: Lock zoom, look-ahead, bounds and supported aspect policy
why: Wider views can expose unpainted edges or change combat visibility.
complete_when: Test all allowed zoom/aspect combinations at map edges; no uncovered scenery or inaccessible targets; reset is predictable.

task: Make world picking and aiming use the same camera transform
why: A correct-looking cursor can still target the wrong ground position.
complete_when: Click/aim markers coincide with world targets through zoom, resize, elevation and UI scaling; invalid rays fail safely.

task: Define occluder fade and camera obstruction rules
why: Players and warnings must remain visible behind architecture.
complete_when: Walk behind arches, trees and walls; fade/outline is stable, restores correctly and does not reveal unexplored gameplay incorrectly.

task: Preserve readable actors, warnings and labels at default distance
why: Fine art details disappear at the chosen wide view.
complete_when: Review hero/enemy silhouettes, threat shapes, item labels and overhead bars at actual play size, including low-contrast scenes.

task: Keep development overlays separate from shipping HUD
why: Debug checkboxes and pose strips consume the play field.
complete_when: Lab controls are toggleable and absent in release mode; no debug binding conflicts with production controls.

workstream: World geometry, navigation and spatial authority
task: Choose and document one authoritative spatial simulation
why: Duplicate 2D and 3D controllers cause divergence, ghost collision and save defects.
complete_when: One owner updates position/hits/nav; any presentation bridge has tested forward/inverse transforms and elevation rules.

workstream: World geometry, navigation and spatial authority
task: Build gameplay collision independently from painted detail
why: Attractive stones or railings do not automatically define traversable space.
complete_when: Navigation and collision match visible edges; no invisible walls, walk-through pillars or reachable decorative voids.

workstream: World geometry, navigation and spatial authority
task: Specify floors, stairs, slopes, bridges and height-separated routes
why: A screen-space overlap is not enough to model two traversable elevations.
complete_when: Test ascent/descent, edge barriers, path choice, overhead routes, spawn heights and projectile elevation consistently.

workstream: World geometry, navigation and spatial authority
task: Implement reliable navigation queries and crowd movement
why: Dense combat requires routes that remain valid around actors and doors.
complete_when: Paths update after obstacles/doors; enemies avoid permanent jams; startup/nav-ready races are covered.

workstream: World geometry, navigation and spatial authority
task: Define depth sorting, transparent edges and shadows for mixed assets
why: Sprites and meshes can disagree about what is in front.
complete_when: Actors pass before/behind props at every supported direction; no sorting pops, halos, incorrect shadow planes or double shadows.

workstream: World geometry, navigation and spatial authority
task: Define projectile and line-of-sight collision layers
why: Navigation passability and spell obstruction are different rules.
complete_when: Ground, walls, actors, friendly units, triggers and effects have documented masks with tests for each intended interaction.

workstream: World geometry, navigation and spatial authority
task: Implement reliable transitions, spawn recovery and streaming seams
why: Players must not fall out of the world or lose state at a district boundary.
complete_when: Cross each exit both ways, reload near transitions and handle invalid saved positions with a safe canonical spawn.

task: Create a reusable modular architecture kit
why: A full city does not require uniquely sculpting every building.
complete_when: Kit includes aligned walls, roofs, arches, stairs, doors, trims and sockets with consistent scale/pivots and assembly examples.

task: Model only the geometry needed for silhouettes, depth and interaction
why: Flat art is efficient at a distance; foreground structure needs convincing volume.
complete_when: Each environment asset records mesh/card/painted-layer choice, collision and depth requirements; the choice passes the camera test.

task: Author painted surfaces without masking weak geometry
why: Noisy textures cannot repair blocky proportions or missing architecture.
complete_when: Review roofs, arches, door proportions and relief in flat lighting first; then approve texture/material treatment at gameplay scale.

task: Split large painted scenery into maintainable regions and occluders
why: One giant plate is difficult to edit, stream and sort against actors.
complete_when: Source layers, seam overlap, tile/region boundaries and foreground masks are retained; movement shows no visible seams.

task: Build a prop and dressing library with gameplay hierarchy
why: Dense detail can obscure paths, loot and attack warnings.
complete_when: Reusable lamps, banners, carts, foliage and debris have budgets; combat lanes and interactables remain visibly clear.

task: Produce lighting, water, foliage and ambient motion selectively
why: Subtle motion creates life but excessive animation and particles compete with combat.
complete_when: Moving dressing is loop-safe, bounded and quality-scalable; collision/navigation does not drift with visual motion.

task: Design levels around encounters, landmarks and return routes
why: Beautiful scenery alone does not create an engaging ARPG route.
complete_when: Blockout tests validate sightlines, chokepoints, retreat space, NPC access, exploration rewards and recognizable exits.

task: Validate generated/procedural layouts if included
why: Random assembly can create unreachable objectives or unreadable scenes.
complete_when: Conditional generator tests many recorded seeds for connectivity, safe spawns, encounter spacing and art seams; otherwise mark authored-only.

task: Create canonical character sheets and scale references
why: Identity must survive a new model or render method.
complete_when: Warrior/Mage sheets cover proportions, costume, handedness, emblems, face/hair and gameplay silhouette; approved art stays traceable.

task: Choose runtime representation by actor category
why: One universal method may overbuild NPCs or underbuild a gear-changing hero.
complete_when: Actor matrix states sprite, pre-rendered sprite or rigged mesh, with directions, actions, equipment and camera constraints.

task: Build clean topology, UVs and materials for rigged actors
why: Auto-generated geometry may import while deforming badly or wasting memory.
complete_when: Technical review checks joints, normals, UV overlap policy, texture density, materials, hidden surfaces and required LODs.

task: Define skeleton, rest pose, semantic bones and attachment sockets
why: Existing IK and hit tools cannot depend blindly on a new rig's bone names.
complete_when: Versioned mapping includes pelvis/feet/hands, weapon/shield, VFX anchors and optional cape/fingers; import rejects missing required mappings.

task: Design equipment families and body-fit rules
why: Inventory portraits do not produce wearable gear.
complete_when: Each supported body has verified weapon/armor attachments, hide masks, clipping rules and art for equipped/world-drop/UI appearances.

task: Validate armor, hands, cape and weapon deformation across actions
why: A good idle pose can conceal clipping during cast or roll.
complete_when: Inspect extreme frames and full motion; armor stays appropriately rigid, grip reads correctly and residual clipping is explicitly dispositioned.

task: Plan enemy families, silhouettes and shared rigs
why: Reusing a skeleton can save work without making every enemy visually identical.
complete_when: Family matrix separates melee/ranged/caster/boss roles through silhouette, scale, gait and attacks, with measured reuse limits.

task: Define corpse, death and despawn presentation
why: Death visuals affect readability, performance and loot visibility.
complete_when: Corpses settle on the correct surface, stop attacking, release targeting, expose loot and expire under documented limits.

task: Specify a complete action matrix for every playable actor
why: Missing transitions make otherwise good assets feel unfinished.
complete_when: Track idle, start/stop, walk/run, turns/strafe, attack, cast, dodge, hit, death, interaction and weapon variants; unused actions are scoped out.

task: Establish foot contact, stride speed and terrain adaptation
why: Sliding and floating immediately break the reference's grounded appearance.
complete_when: Review slow/fast movement, diagonals, stairs and stops; recorded contacts match travel and acceptable foot/ground error.

task: Choose root motion versus controller motion per action
why: Applying both can double movement or desynchronize combat.
complete_when: Action contract names movement authority; interrupt, low-frame-rate and collision tests show no drift or teleport.

task: Author anticipation, impact and recovery with gameplay events
why: ARPG weight comes from timing and readable commitment.
complete_when: Events align with contact/release, audio and VFX; timing remains correct across supported attack/cast-speed modifiers.

task: Implement animation blending, interrupts and recovery rules
why: Abrupt transitions or uncancellable states make input feel unreliable.
complete_when: State graph covers death, stun, roll, skill cancel, movement restart and pause; no stuck or impossible blended poses.

task: Set directional sprite export standards when sprites are used
why: Frame padding and inconsistent pivots cause visible popping.
complete_when: Define directions, mirroring exceptions, frame order, FPS, per-action bounds, foot pivot, light direction and atlas padding.

task: Validate sprite or retargeted motion frame by frame and in playback
why: Generated motion can drift in costume, anatomy, weapons or ground contact.
complete_when: Review loops, first/last frames, every facing and cross-action transitions; correct defects before runtime approval.

task: Test animation readability at the actual camera distance
why: A detailed animation may collapse into an unreadable blur at 120 pixels tall.
complete_when: Silhouette and attack direction remain recognizable in normal-speed play; add purposeful poses rather than global sharpening.

workstream: Input, combat feel and hit resolution
task: Specify input priority, buffering and repeat behavior
why: Responsive control requires explicit handling of overlapping actions.
complete_when: Test held attack, click movement, WASD, queued skills, pause and UI focus; record input-to-action timing at supported frame rates.

workstream: Input, combat feel and hit resolution
task: Implement movement, collision sliding and targeting consistently
why: Movement must remain predictable around corners and enemies.
complete_when: Click and keyboard movement reach intended locations without oscillation; target lock/aim assists have clear acquisition and release rules.

workstream: Input, combat feel and hit resolution
task: Define each attack's shape, range and validation time
why: A visually similar slash can have very different hit behavior.
complete_when: Data defines sweep/cone/projectile/AOE, active interval, line-of-sight and per-target repeat policy; debug geometry matches outcomes.

workstream: Input, combat feel and hit resolution
task: Specify dodge, invulnerability, cooldown and cancel rules
why: A dodge is a combat mechanic, not only a roll animation.
complete_when: Tests cover blocked directions, active swings, resource states, pause/death, repeated input and exact protected/unprotected intervals.

workstream: Input, combat feel and hit resolution
task: Make damage/status application stable under frame-rate variation
why: Dropped frames must not miss projectiles or apply a hit twice.
complete_when: Fixed simulation or swept queries resolve fast attacks; test low/high FPS, pause/resume and many simultaneous contacts.

workstream: Input, combat feel and hit resolution
task: Add controlled hit feedback
why: Impacts need to be felt without obscuring play or causing discomfort.
complete_when: Combine reaction, sound, short VFX and optional shake/hit pause; accessibility settings reduce these independently.

workstream: Input, combat feel and hit resolution
task: Define death, respawn and failure costs
why: Players need understandable recovery and consistent persistence.
complete_when: Death cancels attacks, releases targets, applies only approved penalties, restores a valid state and cannot duplicate items.

task: Create a stable skill registry and authoring schema
why: Hardcoded one-off spells do not scale or support safe saves.
complete_when: Each skill has a validated ID, tags, costs, timing, targeting, animation, effects, icon and localization references.

task: Specify all six AOTL attributes and derived statistics
why: Familiar names do not establish their actual mathematical effects.
complete_when: Document Strength, Dexterity, Vitality, Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma contributions plus health, mana, armor, resistance and other implemented stats.

task: Define modifier order and stacking in one rules specification
why: Tooltip and combat disagreement undermines build decisions.
complete_when: Worked examples cover flat/additive/multiplicative terms, conversion, penetration, crit, resistance bounds, rounding and temporary modifiers.

task: Design level and gear scaling with explicit curves
why: Uncontrolled multipliers cause useless early items or runaway damage.
complete_when: Plot player/enemy health, damage, defense and resource costs across intended levels; test low/high gear and edge-case builds.

task: Define status effects, immunities and crowd-control limits
why: Ambiguous stacking produces stun locks and balance exploits.
complete_when: Specify duration, refresh/stack rules, ownership, cleanse, boss exceptions and visual indicators; tests cover overlapping sources.

task: Plan skill acquisition, mastery and respec rules
why: Progression needs understandable choices and recovery from mistakes.
complete_when: Unlocks, prerequisites, costs, reset behavior and saved state are documented and visible in UI.

task: Build a deterministic balance sandbox
why: Real tuning needs repeatable encounters and calculations.
complete_when: Seeded test scenarios compare time-to-kill, survival, resource sustain and build extremes; designer can change data without editing core code.

task: Reconcile displayed descriptions with actual rules
why: Accurate tooltips are essential in a gear-driven game.
complete_when: Tooltip values use the same evaluated stats as combat and identify conditional effects, cooldowns and unsupported calculations.

task: Build distinct enemy roles and readable intentions
why: Enemy variety comes from behavior, not only recolored models.
complete_when: Melee pursuer, ranged attacker and caster demonstrate different positioning, windup and counterplay in the slice.

task: Specify perception, aggro, leash and reset states
why: Broken pursuit can trap players or allow trivial exploits.
complete_when: Test occlusion, lost targets, unreachable players, returning home, boss reset and player death/teleport.

task: Implement crowd navigation and attack coordination
why: Dense packs become unfair when all actors occupy one point or attack simultaneously.
complete_when: Spawned groups maintain usable spacing, avoid permanent jams and obey encounter attack-pressure limits.

task: Author warnings with clear timing and ground placement
why: Threats must remain readable beneath VFX and on slopes.
complete_when: Telegraph geometry matches damage footprint and impact time; distinguish safe/unsafe space beyond color alone.

task: Build elite and boss state machines with recovery paths
why: Phase transitions and interrupts are common progression blockers.
complete_when: Test threshold crossings, simultaneous effects, death during transitions, arena exits, restart and reward delivery.

task: Author encounter budgets and escalation
why: PoE-like density needs pacing and performance discipline.
complete_when: Each encounter records actor count/roles, spawn waves, recovery space, reward budget and target difficulty.

task: Handle population persistence and farming policy
why: Reloads and respawns affect both challenge and economy.
complete_when: Define what resets, when enemies/containers respawn and how boss/quest rewards avoid duplication.

task: Reconcile the canonical item taxonomy into validated data
why: Artwork names and guesses must not define gameplay categories.
complete_when: Every base item has a stable type, slots, requirements, footprint, stack rule, rarity and art mapping with no orphan IDs.

task: Make grid occupancy match canonical item dimensions
why: Incorrect hit rectangles break placement and trust.
complete_when: Rings/amulets occupy 1×1; one-handed swords 1×3 vertical; test every type at bag edges, overlapping items and save/load.

task: Implement atomic equip, swap, unequip and transfer
why: Partial moves can duplicate or destroy valuable items.
complete_when: Full bags, incompatible slots, two-handed/offhand conflicts, requirement loss and failed operations leave inventory in a valid state.

task: Plan ground drops, labels, pickup range and loot filtering
why: Dense loot needs readable, reliable interaction.
complete_when: Labels avoid blocking combat unnecessarily; ownership/range rules are enforced; filtering cannot hide required quest items without recovery.

task: Design base stats, affix pools, tiers and rarity rules
why: Meaningful loot needs controlled combinations and understandable value.
complete_when: Seeded generation validates level eligibility, mutually exclusive affixes, roll bounds and representative build usefulness.

task: Implement crafting, upgrading and vendor transactions within scope
why: Resource sinks need clear outcomes and exploit resistance.
complete_when: Preview costs/results; apply atomic transactions; test insufficient currency, full bags, cancellation and repeated input.

task: Define currencies, sinks, drop rates and sell values
why: An economy can collapse through inflation or an obvious conversion loop.
complete_when: Simulate expected income/spend across progression, check circular-profit exploits and tune scarcity using playtest evidence.

task: Connect visual equipment changes to supported item families
why: Promising every item a unique appearance multiplies production costs.
complete_when: Document which items share appearances; supported combinations have fitted assets and correct weapon, shield and clothing visibility.

task: Design stash, sorting, comparison and search behavior
why: Inventory management can overwhelm the combat loop.
complete_when: Within approved scope, test quick transfer, sort stability, tooltip comparison, stack splitting and controller navigation without item loss.

task: Define the complete player journey and reward cadence
why: A hub and combat test do not form a finished game.
complete_when: Map tutorial, first build choice, milestones, difficulty changes, narrative beats and a reachable ending or declared sandbox loop.

task: Implement quest state and objective contracts
why: Objectives must survive out-of-order actions and reloading.
complete_when: Stable IDs and state transitions handle pre-collected items, duplicate events, abandonment, death and loading without blocking completion.

task: Build useful NPC services and interaction feedback
why: Service art needs reliable gameplay functions.
complete_when: Approach/hover prompts, dialogue, shops, crafting and quest offers reflect actual availability and cannot activate through blocking UI.

task: Connect narrative delivery to play without requiring full voice-over
why: AOTL needs coherent characters while voice scope stays selective.
complete_when: Written dialogue, journal, environmental cues and optional barks work when voice is disabled or unavailable.

task: Specify tutorial and onboarding coverage
why: Experienced ARPG assumptions can conceal basic usability problems.
complete_when: First-time players learn movement, skill costs, dodge, loot, equip, healing and return-to-hub through tested prompts.

task: Define endgame, replay or campaign-completion scope explicitly
why: Endless systems can consume a small team's entire schedule.
complete_when: Decide launch end state; if endgame is included, specify repeatable activities, modifiers, rewards, difficulty ceilings and retention without content promises.

task: Implement the approved corner HUD using live state
why: A screenshot-like overlay is not a functioning interface.
complete_when: HP/MP, XP, level, skills, flasks, minimap and quest tracker update correctly; mock values and debug-only panels are absent in release.

task: Use shared layout geometry for rendering and input
why: Buttons that look aligned but click elsewhere cause accidental attacks.
complete_when: Clicks and wheel events on frames, gaps, menus and minimap are absorbed correctly across resolution and UI scale.

task: Keep equipment above the right-side inventory and character stats readable
why: The approved layout should support actual item decisions.
complete_when: Equipment, bag, derived stats and tooltips remain usable at minimum resolution without clipped controls or obscured drop targets.

task: Produce full-square distinct skill art and state overlays
why: Small vague symbols are not the approved visual direction.
complete_when: Every skill fills its square, has a distinct border/silhouette, and remains identifiable at 32/48/64 pixels with cooldown/resource overlays.

task: Resolve bindings and provide rebinding/context rules
why: The reference mockup's keys conflict with existing controls.
complete_when: Publish one action map; rebinding detects conflicts and persists; displayed prompts always reflect the current device and binding.

task: Support chosen controller navigation and input switching
why: Mouse interfaces do not automatically work on a gamepad.
complete_when: If scoped in, test focus order, inventory placement, targeting, prompts and device changes; otherwise document keyboard/mouse-only scope.

task: Provide accessibility settings and redundant cues
why: Color, shake and fine text cannot be the only way to read combat.
complete_when: Adjustable text/UI scale, subtitles, contrast cues, reduced shake/flashes and clear focus indicators are tested; evaluate other needs with players.

task: Build complete settings, pause, save feedback and error states
why: Players need predictable recovery from failed actions.
complete_when: Settings apply/persist/revert correctly; menus explain errors; pause follows game mode; loading and save failure remain recoverable.

task: Implement minimap, quest markers and interaction priority
why: Decorative maps and overlapping prompts can mislead players.
complete_when: Map derives from actual navigable content; markers track valid targets; loot/NPC/door priorities prevent unintended activation.

task: Choose a coherent baked versus dynamic lighting policy
why: Painted shadows can conflict with moving lights and actors.
complete_when: Each material category declares lighting treatment; scenes avoid doubled shading, mismatched direction and floating sprites.

task: Author contact shadows and grounding cues
why: Characters must feel attached to the ground in the wide view.
complete_when: Shadows follow feet/height correctly on slopes and stairs; sprite and mesh actors have comparable grounding.

task: Create a school-specific VFX language
why: Similar wisps make different spells hard to identify.
complete_when: Shape, motion, impact and sound distinguish physical, frost, fire and arcane actions; review at gameplay size in mixed combat.

task: Build effect timelines tied to authoritative action events
why: Visual hits that arrive early or late feel unfair.
complete_when: Windup, release, travel, impact and lingering areas match actual mechanics at variable speed and frame rate.

task: Budget transparency, particles, lights and decals
why: ARPG crowds can become GPU-bound through effects alone.
complete_when: Worst-case encounters stay within measured frame budgets; pooled effects and quality limits do not remove essential danger information.

task: Use restrained grading and post effects
why: Global blur, grain and bloom can erase crisp AOTL art.
complete_when: Compare enabled/disabled settings; UI stays sharp; bloom/exposure preserve warning and actor contrast; reduced-effects mode is legible.

task: Create a prioritized sound-event list
why: Combat and interaction feedback need broader coverage than spoken dialogue.
complete_when: List footsteps by surface, weapon impacts, casts, enemy cues, loot, UI, ambience and music states with asset/event IDs.

task: Implement audio buses, mixing and voice limits
why: Dense combat otherwise masks warnings and clips the output.
complete_when: Separate master/music/SFX/voice controls; prioritize danger cues, cap simultaneous sounds and validate a dense encounter mix.

task: Use Grady only for selected NPC/enemy lines within current permission
why: The user chose a voice and limited scope, not full-character narration.
complete_when: Approved line list includes speaker/context, subtitles and playback rules; no paid or credit-consuming ElevenLabs operation is assumed authorized.

task: Make audio resilient to pause, death, distance and missing files
why: Orphaned speech and repeated barks undermine polish.
complete_when: Dialogue cancels/resumes as designed, subtitles match, cooldowns prevent spam, and the game works with audio disabled.

task: Produce looping ambience, music transitions and loudness checks
why: Harsh loops and inconsistent levels are distracting over long sessions.
complete_when: Check headphones/speakers, loops, transitions, compression and licensing; record human listening review.

workstream: Code architecture, tools and engine configuration
task: Pin engine, renderer and dependency versions
why: A successful import on one tool version may fail elsewhere.
complete_when: Document supported Godot version/export templates, Blender/exporter and package versions; fresh setup runs the canonical scene.

workstream: Code architecture, tools and engine configuration
task: Separate simulation, content data and presentation
why: Replacing sprites with meshes should not rewrite inventory or quests.
complete_when: Clear APIs cover input intents, actor state, ability events and world queries; presentation can be swapped without duplicating authority.

workstream: Code architecture, tools and engine configuration
task: Build validated content registries and stable identifiers
why: Renamed files must not corrupt saves or silently break references.
complete_when: Validation catches missing IDs, invalid stats, absent assets, broken localization keys and unsupported skeleton/material contracts.

workstream: Code architecture, tools and engine configuration
task: Create designer-facing debug and authoring tools
why: Content production becomes expensive if every item requires code changes.
complete_when: Tools visualize hit volumes, nav, elevation, pivots, state, stat derivation and encounter seeds; release builds disable developer privileges.

workstream: Code architecture, tools and engine configuration
task: Define error reporting, logging and graceful fallbacks
why: Missing assets and invalid content should be diagnosable without destroying progress.
complete_when: Errors include version and asset IDs; safe fallbacks preserve state; logs avoid credentials and unnecessary personal data.

workstream: Code architecture, tools and engine configuration
task: Maintain testable boundaries and deterministic fixtures
why: Large scene-only tests can hide race conditions and state leakage.
complete_when: Critical math/transactions have focused tests; integration fixtures wait for real nav/import readiness and use isolated save directories.

task: Define persistent versus transient state
why: Temporary cooldowns or animation states should not accidentally become permanent.
complete_when: Save contract covers character, inventory, quests, world changes and settings; respawn/transient behavior is explicit.

task: Use atomic saves, backup slots and corruption recovery
why: A crash or disk-full condition must not destroy the only character.
complete_when: Fault-injection tests interrupt writing, truncate files and exhaust space; the last valid save or clear recovery path remains available.

task: Version the schema and test real migrations
why: New content and renamed IDs must preserve existing progress.
complete_when: Keep representative old saves; migrate forward with backups, handle missing content, and reject unsupported newer saves safely.

task: Test duplication, loss and transaction interruption
why: Loot, crafting and shop actions are high-value consistency boundaries.
complete_when: Repeated clicks, save/reload and interrupted operations cannot duplicate currency/items or leave equipment ownership inconsistent.

task: Define profiles, reset, import/export and cloud conflict policy
why: Multiple machines and characters can overwrite progress unexpectedly.
complete_when: Implement scoped features with clear identity and conflict handling; destructive reset requires intentional UI confirmation.

task: Choose network topology, session size and authority
why: Retrofitting online combat can require rewriting the simulation.
complete_when: If multiplayer is in scope, specify server authority, client prediction, reconciliation, tick rate, transport and host/disconnect policy.
gate: Decide G0; implement before G4 if included

task: Design secure accounts, ownership and transactions
why: Shared economies cannot trust client-authored inventory or damage.
complete_when: Validate actions server-side, protect credentials, rate-limit abuse and test replay/duplicate transaction handling; offline scope is recorded otherwise.
gate: Decide G0; implement before G4 if included

task: Test latency, packet loss, reconnect and synchronization
why: Local correctness does not imply online playability.
complete_when: Simulated network tests cover movement, hits, loot ownership, joins/leaves, boss state and recovery under an agreed latency matrix.
gate: Decide G0; implement before G4 if included

task: Plan backend capacity, deployment, observability and incident response
why: Online services create recurring cost and operational duties.
complete_when: Load tests, region choice, monitoring, backups, rollback and on-call ownership are budgeted before a public online release.
gate: Decide G0; implement before G4 if included

task: Specify trading, matchmaking and moderation only if included
why: These features add economy abuse, support and community obligations.
complete_when: Scope decision names supported social systems, abuse controls and privacy policy; unbuilt features are not advertised.
gate: Decide G0; implement before G4 if included

workstream: Asset pipeline, provenance and repository operations
task: Keep editable masters separate from runtime exports
why: A PNG or GLB alone may not be sufficient to revise the asset.
complete_when: Preserve layered art, blend/source rigs, textures and prompts alongside versioned runtime exports and reproducible settings.

workstream: Asset pipeline, provenance and repository operations
task: Automate import validation and predictable derived assets
why: Manual resizing/exporting leads to inconsistent results.
complete_when: Check dimensions, alpha edges, pivots, UVs, bone maps, animation names, codecs and texture color space; deterministic conversions are repeatable.

workstream: Asset pipeline, provenance and repository operations
task: Track Higgsfield jobs, licenses and current cost authorization
why: Provider output and historic credit plans do not establish present rights or budget.
complete_when: Record source permissions, tool/model/job revision, quoted/actual cost and output selection; no unauthorized spend or sole reliance on expiring links.

workstream: Asset pipeline, provenance and repository operations
task: Establish naming, folder, LFS and large-file rules
why: Unstructured binary history becomes difficult to review and restore.
complete_when: IDs and paths follow a documented convention; clean clones resolve real assets; exceptions to LFS are intentional and recorded.

workstream: Asset pipeline, provenance and repository operations
task: Make a per-asset acceptance and replacement workflow
why: New art must not silently overwrite approved runtime content.
complete_when: Candidate, approved, retired and fallback assets have explicit mappings; replacement PR includes before/after in-engine captures and rollback.

workstream: Asset pipeline, provenance and repository operations
task: Mirror accepted releases to GitHub and the AOTL Drive destination
why: One cloud provider or a local machine is not a reliable handoff.
complete_when: Verify file sizes/hashes and archive contents after upload; include a human-readable manifest and check a clean restore.

workstream: Asset pipeline, provenance and repository operations
task: Budget generation batches by accepted deliverables
why: More generated images do not equal more usable game content.
complete_when: Track acceptance rate, cleanup hours and cost per approved asset; stop a failing style/rig batch for review before expanding it.

task: Set measured frame, memory and loading budgets
why: Optimization needs a defined device and workload.
complete_when: Record CPU/GPU timings, resident memory, VRAM, load and save durations on chosen minimum hardware, with profiler captures.

task: Adopt provisional targets and then validate them
why: Unsupported performance promises hide unknowns.
complete_when: Start with a proposed 60 FPS/16.7 ms frame target at 1080p; allocate subsystem budgets after profiling and explicitly approve any lower target.

task: Benchmark a representative worst-case encounter
why: An empty plaza is not a useful ARPG performance test.
complete_when: Stress agreed actor/projectile/particle/loot counts, camera zoom and UI; report percentiles and hitches, not only average FPS.

task: Optimize actor updates, pathfinding and physics
why: Dense crowds can exhaust CPU before rendering becomes expensive.
complete_when: Profile tick cost, stagger suitable AI work and use measured broadphase/pooling changes; combat-critical precision is preserved.

task: Optimize meshes, textures, transparency and streaming
why: Both sprites and 3D can exceed memory/bandwidth budgets.
complete_when: Measure draw calls, skinning, texture residency, overdraw and load spikes; use batching, LOD/mips/compression as appropriate.

task: Create quality settings that preserve essential information
why: Low settings must not remove danger cues or interactables.
complete_when: Compare supported presets in the same combat scene; readability, targeting and collision remain identical.

task: Test extended sessions and resource cleanup
why: Short runs miss leaks and unbounded corpse/effect accumulation.
complete_when: Soak tests repeat area transitions, combat, menus and saves; memory stabilizes and no persistent orphan objects accumulate.

task: Maintain a requirements-to-evidence matrix
why: Large assertion counts can still omit a critical player flow.
complete_when: Every checklist acceptance links a test, capture or human review at a specific build; known gaps are explicit.

task: Test the complete core loop manually on native target hardware
why: Headless logic cannot prove visual clarity or comfortable controls.
complete_when: Play fight → loot → equip → skill change → quest → death/recovery → save/reload → return-to-hub on supported platforms.

task: Capture controlled visual regressions and movement reviews
why: Static screenshots cannot reveal foot sliding, clipping or bad transitions.
complete_when: Use fixed scene/camera/settings plus video of turns, stairs, casts, rolls and crowds; approve meaningful changes rather than blindly matching pixels.

task: Cover resolution, scaling, localization and device combinations
why: UI defects often appear outside the developer's default setup.
complete_when: Matrix includes supported aspects, minimum resolution, enlarged text, longest language strings and each input device.

task: Test edge cases, corrupted content and interruptions
why: Real users pause, alt-tab, disconnect devices and close the game mid-action.
complete_when: Exercise focus loss, import failures, missing assets, save interruption, rapid input and invalid state without destructive failure.

task: Run structured combat and usability playtests
why: Automated checks cannot measure fairness, confusion or fun.
complete_when: Observe new and experienced players; record task completion, unclear deaths, inventory friction and build choices; prioritize recurring evidence.

task: Define severity, triage, regression and release-blocking rules
why: Teams need agreement on which defects can ship.
complete_when: No unresolved critical crash, progression blocker or item/save-loss defect; exceptions require a named owner and explicit release disposition.

task: Externalize player-facing text and support formatting
why: Late localization is expensive when strings are embedded in art/code.
complete_when: Stable keys, plural/number formatting, font glyph coverage and text expansion work; right-to-left support follows chosen languages.

task: Maintain licenses and attribution for all shipped assets and tools
why: Reference art, fonts, voice and generated material have distinct rights.
complete_when: Asset provenance includes usage/redistribution terms; no copied WoW/Diablo/PoE assets ship; required notices accompany builds.

task: Review voice consent, provider terms and generated-asset provenance
why: Availability of a voice or model does not imply unrestricted use.
complete_when: Confirm permitted commercial/game use, speaker restrictions and retention rules for selected services before release.

task: Define analytics and crash-reporting data collection
why: Diagnostic data can include identifiers or user content.
complete_when: Collect only needed data, document retention/consent where required, avoid secrets in logs and provide applicable privacy information.

task: Plan age ratings, accessibility/store declarations and regional requirements
why: Distribution obligations can delay a completed game.
complete_when: Producer checks target stores/regions, content rating questionnaires, refund/support terms and required disclosures before submission.

task: Create reproducible automated builds from a clean checkout
why: A working editor scene is not a distributable game.
complete_when: CI pins tools, resolves LFS and exports target packages with version, content manifest, licenses and checksums.

task: Test actual exported binaries and fresh installation
why: Editor-only dependencies and missing resources often appear after export.
complete_when: On a clean supported machine, install/run/play/save/relaunch without developer tools or network unless explicitly required.

task: Validate updates, save compatibility and rollback
why: Patches can break previously working characters or installations.
complete_when: Upgrade representative old versions, verify migrations and restore prior builds/backups according to documented limits.

task: Prepare store/demo/support materials from real gameplay
why: Marketing should represent the shipped experience.
complete_when: Screenshots/trailers show accepted runtime footage; feature claims, controls, system requirements, known limits and support links are accurate.

task: Run a release-candidate checklist and preserve the exact build
why: Rebuilding later may produce a different result.
complete_when: Tag source, archive binaries/source manifests, verify hashes and backups, sign/notarize where needed and record release approval.

task: Plan launch monitoring, hotfixes and player support
why: Development continues after the first download.
complete_when: Assign crash/feedback triage, save-loss response, patch cadence, rollback authority and issue communication channels.

task: Maintain content compatibility and documentation after launch
why: New items, areas and balance patches can invalidate old data.
complete_when: Version content IDs, migration tests, changelogs and handoff updates with each release; retire assets only after dependencies are addressed.

workstream: Staffing, estimates, budget and completion control
task: Assign accountable owners and reviewers to each workstream
why: Unowned work remains unfinished even when tools can generate assets.
complete_when: Every active task has a named owner, reviewer, milestone and capacity allocation; one person may hold several roles.

workstream: Staffing, estimates, budget and completion control
task: Estimate from a completed representative asset and encounter
why: Counting prompts or mesh objects is not a production estimate.
complete_when: Track accepted production, cleanup, integration and QA hours; estimate remaining content using measured throughput and explicit revision reserve.

workstream: Staffing, estimates, budget and completion control
task: Build a dependency-based milestone schedule
why: Parallel art output cannot bypass unresolved camera or rig decisions.
complete_when: Schedule G0–G7 with exit evidence, critical path, staffing capacity and risks; dates remain provisional until throughput is known.

workstream: Staffing, estimates, budget and completion control
task: Maintain a complete operating and production budget
why: Software, asset cleanup, storage, localization and support all cost time or money.
complete_when: Record recurring and one-time costs, current authorized limits, actual spend and stop conditions; service credits are not assumed free.

workstream: Staffing, estimates, budget and completion control
task: Control changes and optional systems
why: An ARPG can expand indefinitely through crafting, trading or endgame ideas.
complete_when: Changes state player benefit, asset/system/test cost and displaced work; launch scope is versioned and conditional tasks get a decision.

workstream: Staffing, estimates, budget and completion control
task: Keep risk, debt and unresolved-decision registers current
why: Hidden technical debt becomes a release blocker.
complete_when: Each risk has likelihood/impact, owner, mitigation and trigger; unresolved source, rig and art-quality issues stay visible.

workstream: Staffing, estimates, budget and completion control
task: Verify the final handoff by an independent clean-start walkthrough
why: A document is useful only if another developer can continue from it.
complete_when: A teammate restores the build, finds sources, imports an asset, runs checks and identifies the next task using the handoff alone.
